definitions.gloss: offer; approach (of work, a role, or a contract)
definitions.explanation: An approach made to someone with a concrete proposal — a job, a transfer, a part in a production, an appearance on a program. From English "offer", but narrower: it is used for work and contracts, not for offers of help or of goods for sale.

examples.japanese: {他社|たしゃ}からオファーが{来|き}ている。
examples.english: I have an offer from another company.

examples.japanese: {条件|じょうけん}が{合|あ}わなかったので、{今回|こんかい}のオファーは{断|ことわ}ることにした。
examples.english: The terms didn't suit me, so I decided to turn down this offer.

notes:
Business and entertainment-industry vocabulary. Also used as a suru-verb (オファーする, to make an offer), though the noun is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- オファーを{受|う}ける: to accept an offer
- オファーを{断|ことわ}る: to turn down an offer
- オファーが{来|く}る: an offer comes in
- {出演|しゅつえん}オファー: an offer to appear (on a program, in a film)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {申|もう}し{出|で}: offer, proposal — plain Japanese, and it can be an offer of help as well as of work
- {内定|ないてい}: informal job offer — specifically a company's advance decision to hire a new graduate
